title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.

examples.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] = 2 + 7 = 9, so the answer is [0,1].

hints: A brute force approach checks every pair of numbers in O(n²) time.
For each number, calculate target - currentNumber.
Store previously seen numbers in a HashMap for O(1) lookup.
Check for the complement before inserting the current element.
intuition: For every number x, we need another number target - x. Instead of searching the remaining array every time, store previously seen numbers in a HashMap. If the complement already exists, we have found the answer immediately.

patternExplanation.name: Complement Lookup using HashMap
patternExplanation.coreIdea: Store visited elements and check whether the required complement already exists.

bruteForce.reason: Every element is compared with every other element.

optimal.reason: Each element is processed once and HashMap operations take O(1) on average.

approaches.name: Brute Force
HashMap (Optimal)

edgeCases.reason: Duplicate values can form the answer.
The HashMap solution works regardless of sign.
Array size can be as small as 2.

pitfalls: Adding the current element before checking its complement.
followUpQuestions: Can you solve it in less than O(n²) time?
What if the array is sorted?
Can you solve it with O(1) extra space?
How would you return all valid pairs?
How would you handle a stream of incoming numbers?

notes.title: HashMap Pattern
notes.description: Store numbers seen so far and check whether the complement exists.

notes.title: Why O(n) Works
notes.description: Each element is processed once and every lookup is O(1) on average.

notes.title: Common Mistake
notes.description: Insert the current element only after checking for the complement.

title: 3Sum
description:
Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.

The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.
hints: Fix one number and solve a Two Sum problem on the remaining array.
Use two pointers after fixing the first element.
Skip duplicate values to avoid repeated triplets.
intuition: After sorting, fix one element. The remaining problem becomes finding two numbers whose sum equals -nums[i]. Use two pointers to efficiently search the remaining array while skipping duplicates.

patternExplanation.name: Sorting + Two Pointers
patternExplanation.coreIdea: Fix one element and use two pointers to find the remaining pair.

optimal.reason: Sorting plus two-pointer scan for each fixed element.

approaches.name: Sorting + Two Pointers (Optimal)

edgeCases.reason: Only one unique triplet should be returned.

followUpQuestions: Can you solve k-Sum using this idea?
How would you count triplets instead of returning them?

notes.title: Foundation of k-Sum
notes.description: 3Sum is the building block for 4Sum and general k-Sum.

notes.title: Duplicate Handling
notes.description: Always skip equal values after sorting.

title: 4Sum
description:
Given an array nums of n integers, return all unique quadruplets [nums[a], nums[b], nums[c], nums[d]] such that:

nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] + nums[d] == target.

The solution set must not contain duplicate quadruplets.
hints: Use two pointers for the remaining two numbers.
intuition: 4Sum extends the 3Sum pattern. Sort the array, fix the first two elements, then use two pointers to find the remaining pair that completes the target sum.

patternExplanation.name: k-Sum Reduction
patternExplanation.coreIdea: Reduce 4Sum into multiple 2Sum problems using sorting and two pointers.

optimal.reason: Two nested loops plus two pointers.

approaches.name: Sorting + Two Pointers (Optimal)

edgeCases.reason: Duplicate quadruplets should not be repeated.
Use long to avoid integer overflow.

pitfalls: Integer overflow when summing four numbers.
followUpQuestions: Can you generalize this to k-Sum?
How would you count quadruplets instead of returning them?

notes.title: Extension of 3Sum
notes.description: Fix one extra element and apply the same two-pointer logic.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on the ith day.

Choose a single day to buy one stock and choose a different day in the future to sell that stock.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve. If no profit is possible, return 0.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6).

hints: Track the minimum price seen so far.
At each day calculate current profit.
intuition: The best selling day depends on the lowest buying price before it. Keep track of the minimum price while traversing the array and compute the profit for every day.

patternExplanation.name: Running Minimum
patternExplanation.coreIdea: Maintain the smallest value seen so far while maximizing the difference.

bruteForce.reason: Try every buy and sell pair.

approaches.name: Running Minimum (Optimal)

pitfalls: Updating minimum price after profit calculation incorrectly.
followUpQuestions: What if multiple transactions are allowed?

notes.title: Greedy Observation
notes.description: Always keep the lowest buying price.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].

The solution must run in O(n) time and without using division.
hints: Combine both to compute the answer.
intuition: For every index, the required product equals the multiplication of all elements before it and all elements after it. Compute prefix and suffix products separately and combine them.

patternExplanation.name: Prefix & Suffix Product
patternExplanation.coreIdea: Build cumulative products from both directions.

bruteForce.reason: Multiply all remaining elements for every index.

optimal.reason: Two passes using prefix and suffix products.

approaches.name: Prefix + Suffix Products

edgeCases.reason: Only one position gets the product of remaining elements.

followUpQuestions: Can you solve it with O(1) extra space?
How would you handle extremely large products?

notes.title: Prefix-Suffix Pattern
notes.description: A classic interview pattern for array transformation.
